newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA PLANS COURT CRACKDOWN ON CRIME.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA PLANS COURT CRACKDOWN ON CRIME.

text.p: The South African government plans to tighten its bail laws and introduce compulsory minimum sentences as part of its drive to crack down on rampant crime, Justice Minister Dullah Omar said on Thursday.
Speaking during debate on his 1997/98 budget in the National Council of Provinces, Omar said there had been growing public concern that some magistrates were granting bail too easily.

"It has been a source of great exasperation to find courts granting bail in various serious murder cases, cases of taxi violence in which numbers of people have been killed and in serious rape cases," he said.
"It seems to be that further legislative intervention is necessary to compel courts to refuse bail in serious cases... (and) a new bail law has been drafted and will be presented to cabinet shortly.
"The introduction of compulsory minimum sentences in respect of certain serious offences is also on the cards," Omar said.
